title: Procedural fluency
subtitle: Flexible, accurate, efficient, and appropriate use of procedures — skill that rests on understanding, not speed for its own sake.

sections.sources: Grounded in NCTM, Principles to Actions (2014) & the five strands of mathematical proficiency.

blocks.text: Procedural fluency is skill in carrying out procedures flexibly, accurately, efficiently, and appropriately — knowing not just how to execute a method but which method fits the situation.

Fluency is more than fast recall. The four words matter: **flexible** (more than one route, chosen wisely), **accurate**, **efficient**, and **appropriate** (the right tool for this problem). A student who can only run one memorized algorithm, slowly and without knowing when it applies, is not yet fluent.
What it looks like in a student

items: Chooses an efficient strategy for the numbers at hand — and can explain the choice.
Executes accurately, and self-checks against reasoning.
Has more than one method available and switches when one is clumsy.
Knows when a procedure applies and when it doesn't.

blocks.text: Fluency built *on* conceptual understanding is durable and flexible. Fluency drilled without it is brittle — fast today, gone next unit. The strands reinforce each other; this one is strongest when it grows out of the “why.”
Instructional practices that build it — and how
These Effective Teaching Practices develop procedural fluency most directly:

rows: The direct driver: students develop a strategy from reasoning, then practice it into flexible, accurate, efficient skill — fluency that lasts.
“Is there a more efficient way?” pushes flexibility and appropriate strategy choice, not just speed.
Monitoring work in progress catches errors early and keeps practice accurate and tied to meaning.
Varied problems give students reasons to apply procedures appropriately — choosing the right tool, not running one by rote.

blocks.text: In the toolbelt, [Number Talks & Strings](/math/approach/number-talks) grow flexible strategies, [Fluency Practice](/math/approach/fluency-practice) builds accuracy and efficiency with monitoring, and [Spiral Review](/math/approach/spiral-review) keeps it sharp over time.
Don't mistake *speed* for fluency. Timed accuracy on one memorized method misses flexibility and appropriateness — two of the four defining features. A student can be quick and still not fluent.
“Is there a more efficient way?” A fluent student can usually find one — and tell you why it's better for these numbers.
